content.alt: 22. No! I Won't! I'll Tell Mom! - Is "don't follow strangers" really enough?
content.text:
Is "don't follow strangers" really enough?

Every parent tells their child to be careful of strangers. But when someone actually approaches at the playground waving candy, a child can easily freeze, not knowing how to act.

More than the vague warning 'be careful,' children need 'specific words and actions' they can pull out right in that moment. And the best way to teach that without frightening them is through a story.

Curious about the plot of this stranger-danger story? Explore the lesson through the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read it with your child and talk about it together. We've gathered many stories about No! I Won't! I'll Tell Mom! covering child safety education, stranger-caution stories, toddler safety stories, and more.

content.alt: 22. No! I Won't! I'll Tell Mom! - Safety education through confidence, not fear
content.text:
Safety education through confidence, not fear

Teaching a child that the world is scary only grows their anxiety. What they truly need is the confidence that 'I can protect myself.'

In a dangerous moment—refusing loudly, not following, and telling a caregiver right away—these three simple actions are the strongest shield to protect a child. Promise-words practiced in advance give a child courage in a real situation.

content.alt: 22. No! I Won't! I'll Tell Mom! - The story of how Hori protected himself
content.text:
The story of how Hori protected himself

In the story No! I Won't! I'll Tell Mom!, Hori wavers for a moment when a strange man at the playground tempts him with candy. But the promise he made with Mom that morning suddenly comes flashing back.

Hori pulls his eyes right off the candy and shouts so loudly the whole playground echoes, "No! I don't follow strangers!" Then, without a backward glance, he runs to Mom and tells her. It's a moment where he protected himself with bravery, not fear.

content.text:
The three promise-phrases learned on Tangobook

The heart of this story is three phrases that are easy for a child to memorize. One, if you don't want to, say "No!" loudly. Two, don't follow—say "I won't!" Three, quickly tell Mom!

Tangobook's story repeats these three phrases like a refrain, helping your child recall them naturally in a dangerous moment. Just by reading along with the story, your child learns how to respond with their whole body.

content.alt: 22. No! I Won't! I'll Tell Mom! - Setting our family's safety promise together at home
content.text:
Setting our family's safety promise together at home

After reading, shout "No! I won't!" out loud together with your child. Repeating it like a game means the voice comes out in a real situation too.

Also set a safety promise just for your family. Talking together about who to tell when there's danger and where to run to helps your child feel more secure. Above all, when your child says "No," praise them big with a "Well done!"

content.text:
Frequently asked questions

Q. How do I do stranger-danger education?

A. Teach the promise that when a stranger says 'come with me,' they say 'No, I won't' and tell Mom. Repeating it playfully, without scaring them, helps your child pick it up naturally.

Q. Is it okay to make my child afraid of all strangers?

A. Rather than making them fear everyone, it's better to teach the rule that they don't follow a grown-up who asks for their help. A stranger-danger story makes safe judgment easy to understand.

Q. My child finds it hard to say no.

A. Practice regularly that when they don't want something, it's okay to say 'No, I won't' loudly. Praising them when they speak up with courage helps the power to use their own voice grow.
